Paths in toolero

Source: R/project-paths.R
project-paths.Rd

The one rule every toolero function follows when it is given a file or folder path. This is the single place the rule is written down; the help page of each function that takes a path shows the same section.

Paths

A relative path is read from the project root, not from the working directory. So save_output(fit, "output/fit.rds", saveRDS) writes into the project's own output/ folder whether you call it from the project root, from a document under reports/, or from a job on an HTCondor execute node. You never need to wrap a path in here::here(). Doing so still works, because here::here() returns an absolute path and absolute paths are used as given.

The project root is found afresh on every call, in this order:

  1. The job's scratch directory, when _CONDOR_SCRATCH_DIR names one. HTCondor sets that variable itself, inside every job.

  2. The nearest folder above the working directory that carries a project marker: the .here file init_project() writes, an .Rproj file, a package DESCRIPTION, or a version control folder such as .git.

  3. The working directory, when neither of the above applies.

Absolute paths (including those starting with ~, or a drive letter on Windows) and URLs such as https:// or s3:// are used as given. .. and ./ are not interpreted, so "../data/x.csv" means the folder above the root; write an absolute path to leave the project. A bare "." means the root itself.

Functions that read are forgiving about older code. A relative path that does not exist at the project root but does exist relative to the working directory is read from there, and a message says so. Functions that write never guess: a relative path is always written under the root.

A few arguments are deliberately left alone:

  • init_project() reads path, config and use_rprofile from the working directory, because the project does not exist yet and so has no root.

  • Under Rscript, resolve_input_path() reads the command line argument as given. Run Rscript from the project root or pass an absolute path.

  • Arguments passed on through ... to another function reach it untouched.

  • Where a default is "beside the input" (qmd_to_r() and generate_kb_xml()), the output follows wherever the input was read from.

Two limits are worth knowing. A project nested inside another project is not supported: the nearest marker wins, which can surprise you when you work from the outer one. And on an execute node ~ and $HOME cannot be trusted ($HOME can be the submit node's path), so prefer relative paths in job scripts.
